sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Áeb, also written Aebh or Aobh, was a heroine of Irish legend. The tale of the Children of Lir names her as the mother who bore the doomed children. She was the daughter of the magician Bodb Derg. Her life ended as she brought her second pair of twins into the world. Her only daughter, Fionnuala, then stepped into her place. Fionnuala became the hero of the tale after the children lost their mother. The death of Áeb carried her childless foster-sister, Aífe, into Lir's household. Aífe worked a curse that changed the children into singing swans.
objective: To record who Áeb was and how her death set in motion the tragedy of the Children of Lir.
